newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan bank closed down by court.
newsitem.headline: Jordan bank closed down by court.

text.p: A Jordanian court has ruled that the troubled Amman Bank for Investment, under Central Bank control since March, should be shut down because of heavy losses, a court official said on Saturday.
The court decision puts a legal seal on a deal with the Central Bank to liquidate Amman Bank for Investment and sell off its banking licence to Jordan's biggest bank, Arab Bank.
Arab Bank has used the licence to set up Jordan's second Islamic bank. It says the Central Bank has agreed to underwrite all Amman Bank for Investment's losses and bad debts.
The court official said that judge Mohammad Tarawneh ruled on Thursday that the bank be liquidated because its losses amounted to 75 percent of its paid up capital.
But the ruling may still be appealed by shareholders, the official said.
The Central Bank took control of troubled Amman Bank for Investment last March, effectively putting the loss-making bank, one of Jordan's six investment banks, under its custody.
The bank has doubtful debts estimated to be in excess of 20 million dinars.
